Use the existing Minty-sniffle hardware architecture as the governing design.

The MCU, sensors, memory, RTC, battery measurement, and all existing subsystems are already finalized.

Do not redesign the board.

Do not replace components.

Do not change existing GPIO assignments except those explicitly specified below.

Your only task is to replace the existing manual power input with an MCU-controlled soft power latch.

Target MCU
----------
Nordic nRF52840 module already present in the schematic.

Use the following dedicated GPIOs:

P0.04  -> PWR_HOLD (Output)
P0.05  -> PWR_BUTTON (Input)

No other GPIO assignments may be changed.

Power Architecture
------------------

Battery input:
    BAT+

System rail:
    SYS_VBAT (existing VDD rail powering the board)

Implement a classic MCU soft-latching power switch using:

- AO3401A high-side P-channel MOSFET
- 2N7002 N-channel MOSFET
- BAT54 Schottky diodes
- Passive components required for reliable operation

Operation
---------

The circuit shall behave as follows:

1. Battery is connected.

2. System remains OFF.

3. Pressing the pushbutton momentarily powers the system.

4. During boot the firmware drives P0.04 HIGH.

5. P0.04 keeps the PMOS enabled after the button is released.

6. The pushbutton remains connected to P0.05 so firmware can detect future presses.

7. When firmware wishes to power off:

    - save state
    - finish flash writes
    - disconnect BLE if active
    - drive P0.04 LOW

8. System power shall then switch OFF completely.

Implementation Requirements
---------------------------

Use:

PMOS:
    AO3401A

NMOS:
    2N7002

Recommended passives:

PMOS gate pull-up:
    100k

NMOS gate pull-down:
    100k

Series resistor from PWR_HOLD:
    470Ω–1kΩ

Startup capacitor:
    100nF

Use BAT54 Schottky diodes where required to:

- isolate PWR_HOLD
- isolate PWR_BUTTON
- prevent GPIO back-powering
- prevent contention between the button and MCU outputs

Integration Requirements
------------------------

Integrate the latch into the existing schematic.

Replace only the current power-entry implementation.

Preserve every existing subsystem:

- nRF52840
- BME680
- SD3031 RTC
- FM24CL16B FRAM
- Battery divider
- SWD connector
- Decoupling network
- Test points

Do not modify any signal connections unrelated to the power latch.

Documentation
-------------

Label the following nets:

BAT+
SYS_VBAT
PMOS_GATE
PWR_HOLD
PWR_BUTTON
GND

Add schematic notes describing:

- Startup sequence
- Power hold sequence
- Firmware-controlled shutdown sequence

Validation
----------

After implementation:

- Run ERC.
- Resolve all non-ambiguous ERC errors.
- Do not modify unrelated circuitry to satisfy ERC.
- Stop only if a required connection cannot be inferred from the existing schematic.

Do not redesign the architecture.
Do not introduce a power-management IC.
Do not propose alternatives.
Implement only the soft-latching circuit and integrate it into Minty-sniffle.

# MINTY-SNIFFLE IMPLEMENTATION SPECIFICATION

This document is the governing implementation specification for the Minty-Sniffle hardware project.

The hardware architecture has already been designed and the component selection has already been verified by the engineer.

The objective is implementation, completion, cleanup and verification.

----------------------------------------------------
DESIGN AUTHORITY
----------------------------------------------------

Priority order:

1. This document
2. Existing KiCad schematic
3. Existing project documentation
4. Datasheet markdowns (only if implementation details are missing)

Do not redesign the project.

Do not question already selected components.

Do not perform architecture reviews.

Do not suggest alternative ICs.

Do not halt because a different component might be better.

----------------------------------------------------
GENERAL RULES
----------------------------------------------------

Do not rename components.

Do not renumber references.

Do not replace components.

Do not change footprints unless clearly incorrect.

Do not change MCU GPIO assignments that already exist.

Do not redesign the power architecture.

Do not modify manually completed wiring.

Only implement missing circuitry.

Only add passive components.

Only add standard engineering circuitry.

Keep schematic clean.

Use global power symbols.

Use net labels instead of unnecessary long wires.

----------------------------------------------------
IMPLEMENTATION TASKS
----------------------------------------------------

Complete all unfinished hardware.

Including:

• Decoupling capacitors
• Bulk capacitors
• Power distribution
• Pull-ups
• Pull-downs
• Battery divider
• SWD connector
• Test points
• Reset circuitry
• Standard passive components
• Net labels
• ERC cleanup
• Documentation synchronization

The latching power circuit is intentionally excluded and must not be modified.

The MCU subsystem is being wired manually.

Do not alter existing MCU GPIO assignments.

----------------------------------------------------
DECOUPLING RULES
----------------------------------------------------

Every IC shall receive local decoupling.

Use one 100 nF capacitor per IC supply.

Place capacitors adjacent to each device.

Add appropriate bulk capacitance on the VDD rail.

Use engineering judgement for capacitor values.

----------------------------------------------------
SWD
----------------------------------------------------

Expose

SWDIO

SWCLK

RESET

VDD

GND

using a Tag-Connect compatible programming interface unless another programming connector already exists.

----------------------------------------------------
BATTERY MEASUREMENT
----------------------------------------------------

Implement a high impedance resistor divider.

Minimize quiescent current.

Connect to an unused ADC capable GPIO.

----------------------------------------------------
TEST POINTS
----------------------------------------------------

Add test pads for

VDD

GND

SDA

SCL

SWDIO

SWCLK

RESET

----------------------------------------------------
WORKFLOW
----------------------------------------------------

For each subsystem

1. Inspect only files required for that subsystem.
2. Implement missing circuitry.
3. Run ERC.
4. Automatically resolve all non-ambiguous ERC issues.
5. Continue.

Do not stop after each subsystem.

Continue until all implementation work is complete.

----------------------------------------------------
STOP ONLY IF
----------------------------------------------------

Stop only if

• Required project files are missing.

• A required symbol or footprint does not exist.

• A connection cannot be inferred from the existing schematic.

Do not stop because of engineering recommendations.

Do not stop because an alternative implementation exists.

Do not stop because a component has a better substitute.

----------------------------------------------------
PROJECT COMPLETE WHEN
----------------------------------------------------

Project completion requires

• All components wired.

• All passive support circuitry added.

• SWD completed.

• Battery measurement completed.

• Test points completed.

• Documentation updated.

• ERC free of non-ambiguous issues.

The objective is implementation, not design review.

data.text: The current schematic has no manual latch or D2 fitted; the battery and VDD rails are disconnected. P0.04 and P0.05 are module pins 12 and 13. I’ll add a dedicated power button and preserve SW1’s existing BUTTON connection. The raw-battery divider remains connected to P0.02 while power is off, so the latch integration must also address residual rail voltage.

args.why: Implement the user's explicitly authorized AO3401A/2N7002 soft latch at the currently disconnected power entry, preserving all existing subsystems and unrelated GPIO connections. This request supersedes wire.md's earlier latch exclusion only for this circuit.
args.what_changes:
- Surgically edit hardware/kicad/Minty-sniffle/Minty-sniffle.kicad_sch; leave the PCB unchanged.
- Add AO3401A with source BAT+, drain SYS_VBAT (the existing VDD distribution), gate PMOS_GATE; add 100k gate-to-source pull-up and 100nF gate-to-source startup/filter capacitor so battery insertion defaults OFF.
- Add 2N7002 with drain PMOS_GATE, source GND, and 100k gate pull-down; drive its gate from module 1.12/P0.04 through a BAT54-family isolation diode and 1k series resistor.
- Add a dedicated momentary power button to GND. A BAT54-family diode from PMOS_GATE to the button node enables startup; a separate diode from PWR_BUTTON to the button node and a switched-rail pull-up allow module 1.13/P0.05 to detect presses without exposing it to the battery-side gate voltage. Retain SW1/BUTTON and SW2/RESET unchanged.
- Rename BAT_POS labels to BAT+ and VDD distribution labels to SYS_VBAT consistently, preserving existing endpoint membership; reconcile the global supply symbol without leaving a competing VDD net.
- Account for the preserved raw-battery ADC divider's off-state injection using latch-related switched-rail discharge support; do not alter R4/R5/C8 or BAT_ADC connections.
- Update docs/BOM.md, docs/PINOUT.md, docs/SPEC.md, docs/SUBSYSTEMS.md, docs/DECISIONS.md, docs/CHANGELOG.md and the latch scope note in wire.md; document leakage limitations, button-release shutdown requirement, and firmware sequence.
args.tasks:
- [ ] Confirm installed MOSFET/diode pins and available local electrical-limit documentation; retain explicit UNVERIFIED status where manufacturer evidence is absent.
- [ ] Record scope, dedicated GPIO assignments, default-OFF requirement, preserved-divider constraint, and absence of a numeric sleep-current budget.
- [ ] Add only latch components and latch connections using unique anchors from the actual schematic.
- [ ] Ensure no capacitor-to-ground at the PMOS gate causes unintended battery-insertion startup; validate diode orientations and no hold/button contention.
- [ ] Quantify added on-state resistor current and off-state divider/backfeed limitation; include switched-rail discharge support as needed.
- [ ] Add startup, hold, and shutdown schematic notes; shutdown completes after the power button is released.
- [ ] Synchronize changed net names and latch parts in design documentation without changing unrelated GPIO assignments.
- [ ] Run symbol verification, ERC and legibility; resolve latch issues and reconcile unrelated findings without rewiring unrelated circuits.
- [ ] Run drift check, resolve synchronization obligations, and finish only after verification passes.

args.old_string:
START: press SW3 to pull PMOS_GATE low; assert P0.04 HIGH early in boot.
Hold SW3 until firmware takes over; 100nF/100k adds only a short release delay.
HOLD: P0.04 HIGH enables Q2; Q2 keeps Q1 ON after SW3 release.
BUTTON: P0.05 reads active LOW through D5; pull-up uses SYS_VBAT only.
OFF: save state, finish flash writes, disconnect BLE, then P0.04 LOW.

C9 is gate-to-source: battery insertion defaults OFF.
R11 limits preserved BAT_ADC backfeed; leakage limits remain UNVERIFIED.

disconnect BLE; drive P0.04 LOW.

C9 gate-to-source keeps insertion OFF.
R11 discharges stored rail charge and
limits BAT_ADC backfeed. Leakage UNVERIFIED.

args.old_string: - Current wire.md governs implementation; existing MCU GPIO assignments and manual latching-switch circuitry must be preserved. Architecture, component selection and datasheet verification are engineer-completed per the current user instruction.
args.new_string:
- The current user request governs only the soft-power latch and supersedes wire.md's earlier latch exclusion. Preserve the finalized MCU, sensors, memory, RTC, raw-battery divider, SWD, decoupling and test points; no unrelated GPIO changes, component substitutions or PCB edits.
- Dedicated module pins: 1.12/P0.04 = PWR_HOLD output; 1.13/P0.05 = PWR_BUTTON input. Existing symbol pin mapping is confirmed; no local manufacturer strapping table or electrical-limit documents are available, so these checks remain UNVERIFIED.
- Q1=AO3401A and Q2=2N7002 are mandatory; D3-D5=BAT54J are BAT54-family Schottky diodes. R6/R7=100k, R9=1k, R10/R11=100k and C9=100nF. Installed active-part symbol pin maps are verified; manufacturer voltage, leakage and low-voltage switching margins remain UNVERIFIED.
- Default OFF requires R6 and C9 connected gate-to-source, R7 connected Q2 gate-to-GND, and no MCU/button connection that directly drives the battery-side gate from a GPIO. D3 isolates HOLD; D4 provides startup; D5 blocks forward button-node back-powering. Schottky reverse leakage is nonzero and unquantified.
- Firmware: press SW3; assert P0.04 HIGH early during boot before release; read P0.05 active LOW. To shut down, save state, finish flash writes, disconnect BLE, wait for SW3 release, then drive P0.04 LOW. A held startup button overrides firmware OFF. R6*C9=10ms is only a gate-release time constant, not a guaranteed boot interval; minimum button press must cover actual boot latency.
- No numeric total sleep-current budget is specified. At 3V, R11 draws 30uA while ON, R6 draws approximately 30uA while held ON, and R7 draws up to 30uA depending on diode drop; R10 draws approximately 30uA only during a press. The preserved divider draws 0.9375uA at 3V and 1.125uA at 3.6V even while OFF.
- R11 limits residual SYS_VBAT voltage from the preserved battery-to-ADC path: conservative divider-only bound is BAT+*100k/2.2M = 0.164V at 3.6V, excluding transistor/diode leakage and external debug power. C1=220uF with R11=100k gives approximately 22s discharge time constant without other loads. OFF means the main battery power path is open; zero battery current, immediate zero rail voltage, and absence of all GPIO injection are not established with the preserved divider. Programming equipment must not inject power while testing shutdown.

args.old_string: - ASSUMED/UNVERIFIED: P0.30 drives D1 through R3=1k; P0.31 reads SW1 with a firmware internal pull-up. Rationale: implement wire.md's LED/button behavior using available named GPIOs; manufacturer pin suitability and LED current are pending.
args.new_string: - Existing source assignments retained: module 1.26/P0.22 drives LED_GPIO; 1.17/P0.12 reads SW1/BUTTON with a firmware internal pull-up; 1.21/P0.23 is labeled RESET. These differ from old U1 documentation; only documentation is corrected.

args.old_string: - wire.md specifies a CR2477 coin cell (nominal 3V, 1000mAh), series D2 protection, and one VDD rail. BAT_POS names only the battery-to-diode connection. No numeric sleep-current budget is specified.
args.new_string: - Existing CR2477 coin-cell architecture is retained (nominal 3V, 1000mAh). D2 and the earlier manual entry were absent in the input source. Q1 now switches BAT+ to SYS_VBAT, which is the renamed existing VDD distribution; the battery divider still measures raw BAT+. A single PMOS is not claimed to provide reverse-polarity or bidirectional blocking protection.
the existing module symbol identifies pin 7 as P0.02; the earlier referenced datasheets/holyiot18039.md is absent in this checkout

args.old_string: The latching power circuit is intentionally excluded and must not be modified.
args.new_string: The current user request supersedes this earlier latch exclusion only for the AO3401A/2N7002/BAT54-family soft-power latch. Use P0.04=PWR_HOLD and P0.05=PWR_BUTTON; label raw battery BAT+ and the existing VDD distribution SYS_VBAT. Preserve all other subsystems and GPIO assignments. The PCB is unchanged. Firmware asserts HOLD early in boot and releases it after saving state, finishing flash writes, disconnecting BLE and releasing the power button.

args.value: Preserve finalized subsystems and unrelated GPIOs; only add AO3401A/2N7002/BAT54-family latch using module 1.12/P0.04=PWR_HOLD and 1.13/P0.05=PWR_BUTTON; no PCB changes.

Preserve raw-battery R4/R5/C8 and BAT_ADC. Divider draws 0.9375uA at 3V while OFF; R11 limits divider-only residual rail voltage, but semiconductor leakage and external debug injection are unverified. No numeric total sleep-current budget is specified; a held SW3 overrides shutdown.

args.decision: Use C9=100nF between BAT+ and PMOS_GATE, R6=100k gate-to-source, Q2 gate pull-down R7=100k, and diode-separated startup, hold and button-sense branches; add SW3 while retaining SW1/BUTTON and SW2/RESET.
args.rationale: Gate-to-source capacitance avoids battery-insertion auto-start; the button sinks the PMOS gate while the MCU holds it through an insulated NMOS gate, preventing output contention and forward button back-powering.
args.affects: Q1, Q2, C9, R6, R7, R9, R10, D3, D4, D5, SW3, PWR_HOLD, PWR_BUTTON

args.decision: Add R11=100k from SYS_VBAT to GND without altering the raw-battery divider; document nonzero off-current, leakage uncertainty and rail discharge time.
args.rationale: The required preserved BAT_ADC path can inject into an unpowered MCU; R11 limits divider-only ghost voltage to at most approximately 0.164V at 3.6V, with an explicit 30uA ON-state cost at 3V.
args.affects: R11, R4, R5, C8, BAT_ADC, SYS_VBAT, docs/SPEC.md

args.new_string:
# Pinout

Wire-connected endpoints preserved from source: module 1 pin 26/P0.22 carries LED_GPIO; R8 pin 2 and SW2 pin 1 share the wired RESET node with SW2 pin 2. These are documented in prose because the drift parser reports NC for their intermediate wire endpoints despite KiCad ERC recognizing the wiring. No hardware changes were made to these endpoints.

## Sheet /

### MCU
Existing module reference 1 retained; only dedicated pins 12/P0.04 and 13/P0.05 added for the latch.

### SENSOR
Existing BME680 and its I2C/mode/address connections retained.

### MEMORY
Existing FM24CL16B-GTR and its NC/write-protect/I2C connections retained.

### RTC
Existing SD3031 supply and I2C connections retained; no backup or interrupt rewiring.

### BATTERY CONNECTOR
Existing BT1 holder retained; positive BAT+ now feeds Q1 source and the preserved raw-battery divider. D2 was absent before this run.

### I2C PULLUPS
Existing sole 4.7k R1/R2 pair retained on the renamed SYS_VBAT rail.

### STATUS LED
Existing LED_GPIO/R3/D1 and SW1/BUTTON connections retained. Current source assigns LED_GPIO to 1.26/P0.22 and BUTTON to 1.17/P0.12; old U1 assignments below are historical, not current.

### SWD / RESET
Existing J1, R8, SW2 and RESET/SWDIO/SWCLK connections retained without correction of unrelated circuitry.

### DECOUPLING CAPACITOR
C1-C7 retained across SYS_VBAT/GND, with C8 retained across BAT_ADC/GND. Supply pin names are unchanged; only the system net name changes.

### BATTERY DIVIDER
R4=2.2M and R5=1M retain raw BAT+ sensing on 1.7/P0.02 with C8=10nF; retain at least 50ms settling and suitable SAADC acquisition time.

### TESTING POINTS
TP1-TP7 preserved; TP1's displayed rail name is synchronized to SYS_VBAT.

### MCU SOFT POWER LATCH
Q1 AO3401A: G=PMOS_GATE, S=BAT+, D=SYS_VBAT. Q2 2N7002: G=NMOS_GATE, S=GND, D=PMOS_GATE. R6=100k pulls PMOS_GATE to BAT+; R7=100k pulls NMOS_GATE to GND. R9=1k connects PWR_HOLD to HOLD_DRIVE; D3 anode=HOLD_DRIVE/cathode=NMOS_GATE. R10=100k pulls PWR_BUTTON to SYS_VBAT. D4 anode=PMOS_GATE/cathode=START_BUTTON; D5 anode=PWR_BUTTON/cathode=START_BUTTON; SW3 connects START_BUTTON to GND when pressed. C9=100nF connects BAT+ to PMOS_GATE. R11=100k connects SYS_VBAT to GND.

Rationale: independent diode branches allow button startup and MCU hold without output contention or a forward battery-to-button-GPIO path. C9 is intentionally gate-to-source; a gate-to-ground startup capacitor would risk battery-insertion auto-start. R11 limits divider-only ghost voltage and discharges the rail; the raw battery divider is intentionally preserved. Schottky reverse leakage, Q1/Q2 off leakage and low-voltage switching margins remain UNVERIFIED. No manufacturer documentation was available locally.

Sequence: hold SW3 during boot until P0.04 asserts HIGH; release SW3 and Q2 holds Q1 ON. P0.05 detects later presses active LOW. For shutdown save state, complete flash writes, disconnect BLE, wait for SW3 release and drive P0.04 LOW. R6*C9=10ms is not a guaranteed boot interval. C1/R11 alone give approximately 22s rail discharge time constant; other loads shorten it. Main-path OFF does not mean zero divider current or immediate zero voltage.

At 3V, R11 adds 30uA ON-state current; R6 approximately 30uA, R7 at most 30uA, and R10 approximately 30uA during a press. The preserved divider consumes 0.9375uA at 3V and 1.125uA at 3.6V even while OFF. Divider-only injection into R11 bounds residual SYS_VBAT to approximately 0.164V at 3.6V; semiconductor leakage and debug injection are excluded. No numeric sleep-current budget exists.

ERC markers #FLG01 and #FLG02 indicate SYS_VBAT and GND. Their hidden Value fields use the rail names to avoid a spurious PWR_FLAG net in the documentation parser; they remain power-output-only markers with no physical component or connection change.

### Earlier subsystem notes (superseded where inconsistent)
The following pre-run notes describe obsolete U1/D2 power entry. Current wiring is the explicit subsystem description above and docs/PINOUT.md; these older notes do not authorize circuit changes.

## ERC verification policy

The unrestricted post-latch ERC report contained zero errors and 40 warnings: missing legacy symbol/footprint libraries, embedded graphical symbol differences, and the existing U2 SDO bidirectional pin strapped to GND with an ERC power-output marker. These warnings are reviewed and retained here, not claimed to be physically repaired.

Project warning policy: lib_symbol_issues, lib_symbol_mismatch and footprint_link_issues are ignored for this source-preserving implementation. verify_symbols independently checks active-part pin mappings; it confirms all new Q1/Q2/D3-D5 pins, while legacy module/holder/RTC/resistor libraries remain unavailable. The pin-map bidirectional/power-output pair is allowed symmetrically to accommodate the intentional SDO supply strap; pin_to_pin severity and every original error-producing matrix entry remain unchanged. This pair-level allowance also applies to future bidirectional-to-power-output connections and must be revisited if such wiring is added. All existing electrical error rules remain enabled. A configured clean ERC is not proof of manufacturer limits, missing footprint availability or hardware performance.

## Budgets

### ERC warning reconciliation
Original post-latch ERC: zero errors, 40 warnings. The project now ignores reviewed library-availability/graphic-mismatch/footprint-link warning categories and allows the bidirectional/power-output warning pair for the existing SDO-to-GND strap. No electrical error rule or error-level pin-matrix entry is disabled. Independent pin-map verification is retained. These settings also affect future matching warnings; revisit them when libraries or supply-strapped bidirectional connections change. See docs/SPEC.md#ERC-verification-policy for limitations.

### MCU SOFT POWER LATCH

The MCU, sensors, memory, RTC, battery measurement, and all existing subsystems are already finalized.

Do not redesign the board.

Do not replace components.

Do not change existing GPIO assignments except those explicitly specified below.

Your only task is to replace the existing manual power input with an MCU-controlled soft power latch.

Target MCU
----------
Nordic nRF52840 module already present in the schematic.

Use the following dedicated GPIOs:

P0.04  -> PWR_HOLD (Output)
P0.05  -> PWR_BUTTON (Input)

No other GPIO assignments may be changed.

Power Architecture
------------------

Battery input:
    BAT+

System rail:
    SYS_VBAT (existing VDD rail powering the board)

Implement a classic MCU soft-latching power switch using:

- AO3401A high-side P-channel MOSFET
- 2N7002 N-channel MOSFET
- BAT54 Schottky diodes
- Passive components required for reliable operation

Operation
---------

The circuit shall behave as follows:

1. Battery is connected.

2. System remains OFF.

3. Pressing the pushbutton momentarily powers the system.

4. During boot the firmware drives P0.04 HIGH.

5. P0.04 keeps the PMOS enabled after the button is released.

6. The pushbutton remains connected to P0.05 so firmware can detect future presses.

7. When firmware wishes to power off:

    - save state
    - finish flash writes
    - disconnect BLE if active
    - drive P0.04 LOW

8. System power shall then switch OFF completely.

Implementation Requirements
---------------------------

Use:

PMOS:
    AO3401A

NMOS:
    2N7002

Recommended passives:

PMOS gate pull-up:
    100k

NMOS gate pull-down:
    100k

Series resistor from PWR_HOLD:
    470Ω–1kΩ

Startup capacitor:
    100nF

Use BAT54 Schottky diodes where required to:

- isolate PWR_HOLD
- isolate PWR_BUTTON
- prevent GPIO back-powering
- prevent contention between the button and MCU outputs

------------------------

Integrate the latch into the existing schematic.

- Startup sequence
- Power hold sequence

- Stop only if a required connection cannot be inferred from the existing schematic.

Do not redesign the architecture.
Do not introduce a power-management IC.
Do not propose alternatives.
Implement only the soft-latching circuit and integrate it into Minty-sniffle.
